HANDOFF FROM T-101 (cycle 4), three things this item now owns:
(1) RESOLVED-STATUS CONVENTION. KI-1 and KI-6 are both in state.json resolved_issues, but REPORT.md's Known Issues table still LISTS them as rows (KI-1's row now carries the completed finding at severity low; KI-6's row still reads as open). (2) The table header still says 'Known issues (7)'. If rows move out, the count moves with them.
(3) RESIDUAL flagged by the T-101 gate, not fixed there because it was outside that item's acceptance: README.md line ~27 opens 'Most terminal moon phase tools compute the phase with a naive synodic-month modulo, which drifts by hours to days.' The sweep substantiates that for ONE package (the nearest), not for 'most', and 'hours to days' is an unsourced pre-existing magnitude. The standing no-unsourced-numbers rule says a quantity may appear only in the frame the repo already computes it in. Either source it, scope it to the one package the sweep actually examined, or drop the magnitude.

DEP UPDATE cycle 8: T-103b is now done. T-108's remaining open dep is T-109.

DEP UPDATE cycle 9: T-109 is now done. ALL DEPS CLOSED - T-108 is unblocked and is the highest-value item left on the backlog.

.swarm/runs/cycle-010-verify-T-108.txt). Four of six checks passed; two failed, both
inside the run's doc-truth premise.

WHAT PASSED and must be REPRODUCED, not rediscovered — attempt 1 got these right:
 - The status-column table renders correctly and the severity column stayed severities.

FAILURE 1 — false quantity. Attempt 1 wrote "all 8 commits have been pushed" (KI-3 row)
and "Eight commits have been pushed" (hand-off item 4). `git rev-list --count HEAD` = 24.
The figure was carried out of line 5, where "8 commits" truly records the ORIGINAL run,
and restated in the present tense as a total covering the repo now. "all 8" asserts a
complete inventory, so a reader concludes 16 commits do not exist. The retry must not
state a commit total at all unless it counts one at write time; the honest sentence needs
no number. Hand-off item 4's bold lead-in "**Push it somewhere.**" is an instruction to a
human to do something already done and must go with it.

FAILURE 2 — misattributed magnitude in README (the residual half of this item). Attempt 1
wrote "`lunarphase-js` computes the phase with a naive synodic-month modulo - one that
lands nearly four hours off on the 2000-01-06 new moon". The four-hour figure is computed

repo's mean-phase formula. lunarphase-js was never run and per the SPEC's Domain rules
uses a different epoch and synodic constant, so the figure is not that package's error.
This is verbatim the T-101 attempt-1 defect the cycle-4 decision recorded. Removing the
"most tools" generalization and then pinning the same borrowed magnitude onto one named
package makes it read MORE authoritative, not less.

FAILURE 2b — self-contradiction. After the rewrite, "It draws the moon from a fixed set of
sprites, which is backwards for the southern hemisphere" binds "It" to lunarphase-js,
while the next paragraph says that package has "hemisphere support that swaps emoji
glyphs". Two sentences apart the file says the package both lacks and has hemisphere
handling. Rebinding the subject from a general class to a named package was the required
fix; carrying the general class's predicate along with it was not.

items.title: The KI-7 domain doc comment glosses a half-open interval as an inclusive year range
items.acceptance: All THREE places that describe the KI-7 supported domain agree with the half-open interval the constant actually defines - endMs is Date.UTC(3000,0,1) EXCLUSIVE, and test/astro.test.js's loop runs i=0..3999 so its largest sample is strictly below it, meaning calendar year 3000 is NOT covered: (1) src/astro.js's PHASE_ILLUMINATION_CONSISTENCY_DOMAIN doc comment, which currently glosses it as 'calendar years 1000 through 3000' one line above stating the interval correctly; (2) README.md's ## Accuracy paragraph, 'Over years **1000-3000**'; (3) REPORT.md's KI-7 row, 'calendar years 1000-3000'. The constant, the test, and the sample count must not change - only the prose that describes the interval.
items.notes:
FOUND BY THE T-103b GATE at cycle 7, in the module rather than in the item under test. The comment reads 'calendar years 1000 through 3000 (i.e. [Date.UTC(1000,0,1), Date.UTC(3000,0,1)))'. The bracket notation is correct and self-documenting; the prose gloss before it is off by one calendar year at the top end. Low value - the interval notation sits immediately beside the gloss, so a careful reader is not actually misled - but it propagates: T-103b is required to match the module, so the module's imprecision would be copied into README by construction. Fix the module and the README inherits the correct frame.
DELIBERATELY NOT bundled into T-103b: that item's acceptance is 'the domain figures must match the module constant exactly', and letting a docs builder silently re-scope the module's own claim is the opposite of the discipline this run is enforcing.
SCOPE WIDENED cycle 11. T-108 sourced REPORT.md's new KI-7 row to the constant as briefed, and thereby propagated the constant's own inclusive-sounding gloss into a third file. The cycle-11 gate ruled this a defect of the gloss, not of T-108: the builder restated the repo's own declared domain faithfully, and the pre-existing README line says the same thing and passed the cycle-8 gate. Fixing one site and leaving two would leave the repo contradicting itself, so all three move together.
WAVE NOTE: now overlaps T-111, T-113 and T-114 in README.md. No two of those four may share a wave.
DONE cycle 17. Conductor gate: diff scope prose-only across the three named files (constant and test/astro.test.js outside the diff); a conductor-authored discriminator importing the shipping constant and re-reading SAMPLE_COUNT out of the test showed last sample 2999-07-02 < endMs, year 3000 outside the domain, years 1000 and 2999 inside - so the new framing is a fact about both the constant and the test, and the old gloss was false; grep confirms no unqualified inclusive gloss survives in any shipped file; 113/113 green on merged main; CLI smoke clean. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-017-verify-T-110.txt

items.title: Propagate the KI-1 prior-art finding into README and REPORT
items.acceptance: README's differentiation claim and REPORT's KI-1 row both state the completed prior-art finding verbatim from SPEC.md (nearest npm package lunarphase-js v2.0.3 is a naive mean-synodic modulo with zero periodic corrections and emoji-only 'hemisphere support', not a CLI; astronomia v4.2.0 is a genuine Meeus port deliberately not adopted as a dependency) in place of the old 'never swept / permission-blocked' language.
items.notes:
PLAN grep (conductor-verified): zero hits for lunarphase-js|astronomia|prior-art in README.md; REPORT.md's KI-1 row still reads 'never swept... permission-blocked', which is now stale. The finding is written out in SPEC.md 'Domain rules' - copy it, do not re-derive it. L-026: never hand-edit captured output.

ATTEMPT 1 FAILED THE GATE (cycle 2), reverted. Model escalated haiku->sonnet. Two defects, both must be avoided on the retry:
(1) GATE-FAILER - FABRICATED MAGNITUDE. The README note asserted the naive modulo gives '4-hour phase errors'. Conductor-verified: the string '4-hour' appears NOWHERE in the repo except the line the builder wrote - not in SPEC.md, not in src/astro.js, not in any prior doc. SPEC's prior-art bullet states 'zero periodic correction terms' and never quantifies the error. It is also probably wrong in the understating direction (Meeus ch.49's single largest periodic term for new/full moon is ~0.40720 d ~= 9.8 h, and the terms sum), so it silently WEAKENS our own differentiation claim while being unverifiable. RULE FOR THE RETRY: state the structural fact (zero periodic corrections vs a full Meeus series) and do NOT quantify the error at all unless the number is computed in-repo and shown.
(2) SHOULD-FIX - the retry put the string 'closed' in the REPORT.md Known Issues table's SEVERITY column, whose other values are medium/low. That conflates status with severity and drops KI-1's real severity (state.json: low). Keep severity a severity; if a resolved-status convention is needed, T-108 owns the table reconciliation - coordinate, do not invent a convention unilaterally here.
CONDUCTOR RULING: this escalation to sonnet must SURVIVE the gear-1 docs demotion rule (which would otherwise push docs items sonnet->haiku). The failure mode was fabrication under the cheaper tier; demoting it back would just reproduce the defect.

ATTEMPT 2 PASSED THE GATE (cycle 4) at sonnet; seven conductor-run checks, evidence in .swarm/runs/cycle-004-verify-T-101.txt. Zero magnitudes introduced (verified by extracting every numeric token from the added lines: only 'KI-1', a list ordinal, and the two SPEC-verbatim version strings v2.0.3/v4.2.0). Severity column holds only severities; KI-1's cell corrected medium->low to match state.json. Stale never-swept language gone from BOTH the table row and the hand-off section. 104/104 green. KI-1 resolved.

CORRECTION TO THE CYCLE-2 RECORD: the stated reason above - that '4-hour' appears NOWHERE in the repo - was a too-narrow grep for the hyphenated literal. The figure IS in-repo in words at README.md:156-157, REPORT.md:34 and test/astro.test.js:96. The gate DECISION was still right: it is a single hand-computed datapoint for the 2000-01-06 lunation, and attempt 1 lifted it into a general per-package error claim about a package nobody ran (understating besides - the largest single ch.49 term is ~9.8h and the terms sum). The retry brief carried this correction so the builder would not be licensed by its own grep.

items.title: Declare the KI-7 supported date domain in src/astro.js and pin it with a SAMPLED consistency test
items.acceptance: src/astro.js exports a named constant declaring an explicit supported date-range domain for phaseName/illumination consistency, with a doc comment stating WHY the two Meeus series (ch.48 elongation vs ch.49 instant tables) are only guaranteed consistent inside it. test/astro.test.js SAMPLES points across that declared domain (sampling, never an exhaustive sweep) and asserts the phase name band-discriminator holds at every sampled point.
items.notes:
SPLIT FROM T-103 at cycle 6 (see state.json decisions). This slice owns the MODULE + TEST; the README sentence is T-103b, which deps on this one so the quantity enters the docs only after the repo computes it (standing docs frame rule, cycles 2/4).

CONDUCTOR-MEASURED at cycle 1 - use this, it is sharper than the KI-7 text. The right invariant is a DISCRIMINATOR (L-024): the phase name's illumination BAND must contain the reported illumination - crescent < 0.5, gibbous > 0.5, new < 0.10, full > 0.90 (quarters straddle, exempt). Observed contradictions outside the domain:
  new Date(4.0e15)  -> 'waning gibbous'  ill=0.0385   (gibbous but 3.85% lit)
  new Date(-8.0e15) -> 'waning crescent' ill=0.8053   (crescent but 80.5% lit)
Measured clean region: 0 violations in 32,004 sampled states from year -2000 to 6000; first violation ~72,500 years from 1970. Recommend declaring year 1000-3000 as the supported domain - comfortably inside the measured-clean region with margin. SAMPLED, not exhaustive (taste judge, scope-fits-night).

SCOPE FENCE: this item does NOT change any astronomy. No edits to truePhaseJD, elongationDeg, lunationK, the correction tables, or any polynomial. Adding a constant plus a doc comment plus a test is the whole job. The core is verified against Meeus 49.a/49.b and the SPEC non-goal forbids rewriting it.

The DISCRIMINATOR is the point (L-024): assert the phase name band CONTAINS the reported illumination, not that illumination equals a remembered value. Bands: new < 0.10, waxing/waning crescent < 0.5, waxing/waning gibbous > 0.5, full > 0.90; first/last quarter STRADDLE and are exempt.

items.title: State the declared KI-7 supported date domain in README, sourced to the shipping test
items.acceptance: README.md states the same supported date domain that src/astro.js declares, names the consequence of leaving it (phaseName and illumination may contradict each other), and attributes the bound to the in-repo sampled test rather than to an unsourced claim. The domain figures must match the module constant exactly.
items.notes:
SPLIT FROM T-103 at cycle 6. Runs AFTER T-103a so the domain is machine-checked before the README asserts it. STANDING DOCS FRAME RULE (cycles 2 and 4): a quantity may appear only in the frame in which the repo already computes it. Here the frame is exactly what T-103a s test samples - a sampled-clean domain - and the README must not widen it into a proof of correctness outside the sample or into a general accuracy claim.

ATTEMPT 1 FAILED THE GATE at cycle 7 (haiku). Reverted with `git checkout -- README.md`; tree returned clean, 106/106 still green. Read this before retrying - the retry brief is written WITH the correction in it so attempt 2 does not re-argue a settled point.

WHAT ATTEMPT 1 GOT RIGHT (keep all of it): scope fence held (README.md only); the domain figures 1000/3000 were copied correctly from src/astro.js:72-73; NO invented magnitudes (every numeral in the added text already existed in HEAD README or src/astro.js); the consequence was named concretely ('phaseName and illumination may contradict each other') rather than hand-waved; 'Outside this domain, behavior is unspecified' is exactly right; the voice matched the surrounding section.

WHY IT FAILED - ONE CLAUSE. It wrote: 'Over years **1000-3000**, `phaseName` and `illumination` are mutually consistent -- confirmed by test/astro.test.js.' The word CONFIRMED, with no sampling hedge anywhere in the added text, states as established a property the repo only sampled. Every other layer of the repo hedges: src/astro.js says 'SAMPLED-clean, not proven ... not a derived error bound'; test/astro.test.js:386 says 'This SAMPLES -- never exhaustively sweeps --'; the test's own name ends in '(sampled)'. The added README sentence was the ONLY place in the repo asserting the consistency unhedged. Measured at the gate: the test checks 4000 points across a 730,485-day domain = one point per ~183 days, 0.548% of the domain's distinct days. 'Confirmed' asserts a property of a continuum from that sample.

THIS IS NOT A STYLE NOTE. Discriminator the gate applied: if the implementation were wrong at some unsampled instant inside 1000-3000, the module doc comment would still be TRUE ('found no contradiction anywhere in the sample') and the README sentence would be FALSE. A docs item whose job is to document a bound must not make a strictly stronger claim than the module it documents.

WHAT ATTEMPT 2 MUST DO: keep the sentence essentially as-is and carry the hedge into it. The bound is what an in-repo test SAMPLED and found no contradiction in - not what it confirmed, proved, guaranteed, validated or verified. Do not pad the paragraph to compensate; this is a one-clause repair, and the gate will re-check scope, figures and magnitudes exactly as before.

RESIDUAL, NOT A DEFECT IN THIS ITEM (do not 'fix' it, do not widen scope to it): the module's own doc comment glosses the half-open interval [Date.UTC(1000,0,1), Date.UTC(3000,0,1)) as 'calendar years 1000 through 3000', so year 3000 itself is outside the domain but reads as inside. Attempt 1 inherited that phrasing verbatim from the module and was NOT failed for it - matching the module constant is this item's acceptance. Logged separately as T-110.

ATTEMPT 2 PASSED THE GATE at cycle 8 (sonnet). Landed text (README.md, appended to ## Accuracy): 'phaseName and illumination come from two different Meeus series, so nothing guarantees they stay in step forever. Over years 1000-3000, test/astro.test.js samples that domain and finds no contradiction between them; outside it, behaviour is unspecified and the two fields may disagree.' items.why: src/args.js toUsageError recovers the offending token from node:util's message with /'([^']+)'/. The `+` requires at least one character, so for an EMPTY positional -- where node:util's message contains '' -- the match fails, `token` falls back to the empty string, and the user-facing sentence loses its subject entirely. Verified end-to-end at the CLI (cycle-34 scan probe 2): `moon ""` exits 2 with stderr `moon: unexpected argument - moon takes no positional arguments; run 'moon --help' ...`, whereas `moon bogus` and `moon "   "` both name their token. This is the one input class where naming the token matters MOST: an empty argument is invisible on the user's command line, so a message that names nothing leaves them with nothing to look at. The realistic shape is not `moon ""` typed by hand but `moon "$MOON_OPTS"` with the variable unset. The code's own comment states the intent it fails here: "node:util quotes the offending token in its message; recover it so we can name it."

items.title: The --json docs describe cycleFraction as temporal ("position through the synodic month") but it is angular (elongation/360) and disagrees with age by up to ~21 hours
items.why: The --json surface is advertised in bin/moon.js HELP as "structured output for scripting (stable, documented below)", so its field descriptions are a contract. cycleFraction is computed at src/astro.js:303 as phaseAngle/360 - an ANGULAR fraction of the elongation circle. `age` (src/astro.js:313) is genuine elapsed days since the true ch.49 new-moon instant. Both the README field table and the HELP fields block describe cycleFraction as "position through the synodic month", which reads as temporal, and nothing warns that the two fields are not convertible. Measured by the conductor over 175,320 hourly samples across 2020-2040 (.swarm/runs/cycle-036-probe-cyclefraction.js): the circular gap between cycleFraction and age/lunation reaches 0.029790 cycle = 21.11 h against this lunation TRUE length, and 0.032488 cycle = 23.03 h against the mean synodic month. So a script computing elapsed days as cycleFraction * 29.53 is wrong by up to most of a day. The repo already carries exactly this kind of correction for exactly this kind of trap - the "Caution on phaseAngle" block - and this is the second such field with no such note. The gap is ALREADY KNOWN to the code: test/astro.test.js:242 pins circDiff(cycleFraction, elapsed/SYNODIC) < 0.035 with the comment "may lead/lag mean time by the periodic corrections (up to ~0.9 d ~ 0.03 cycle)". The test knows; the documentation does not.
items.acceptance: The --json documentation in BOTH README.md and bin/moon.js's HELP string tells a scripting reader that cycleFraction is an angular quantity (the Moon-Sun elongation as a fraction of the circle), NOT elapsed time, and that converting it to days is wrong by up to roughly 21 hours mid-cycle; it directs the reader to the `age` field for elapsed time. The note must also state the part that is true: the endpoints hold - at a true new moon cycleFraction is 0 and at a true full moon it is 0.5, each to within about 0.001 of a cycle (~45 minutes). The two documents must agree with each other. NO behavior change: src/ is untouched and the only edit to bin/moon.js is inside the HELP template literal.

items.title: README's KI-5 limitation makes the reader learn East Asian Width jargon to answer 'am I affected?'
items.acceptance: README's 'Known limitation: terminal glyph width' section lets a reader settle whether their own terminal is affected from something they can observe on screen (a check they can run and an outcome they can compare), without needing to know what 'Neutral' or 'Ambiguous' East Asian Width means or which terminal setting they have. The existing technical explanation stays -- nothing is deleted or weakened; the section gains the missing observable, and the truth of every retained sentence is preserved.
items.notes: Found at cycle 60 (inline PLAN); this is SPEC nice-to-have #2, unlocked now that every must-have is verified. Conductor-verified premise: README.md:205-224 explains the failure via Unicode width classes and names iTerm2's 'treat ambiguous-width as double' and `xterm -cjk_width` as configurations, but nowhere tells the reader what to LOOK AT on their own screen. The section already names an observable a reader could check unassisted (the `--block` frame not closing) -- the gap is that nothing points them at it as the test. Churn guard: rewording the existing paragraphs is NOT this item; if the diff does not add a check a reader can perform, the item is not done. | cycle 62 ATTEMPT 1 FAILED THE GATE (haiku). The attempt added a check keyed on the two right-hand CORNERS lining up with each other. That observable is factually wrong: all six frame glyphs are East Asian Width Ambiguous, so both border rows scale by the same factor and the corners stay aligned with each other in an affected terminal (both at column 66 of a 68-column row); what goes ragged is the right bar on the CONTENT rows (columns 34-37, differing row to row). A reader in an affected terminal would have read the two aligned corners as 'fine'. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-062-verify-t151.txt. Retry must pick an observable that actually differs between the two cases, and must establish that it does before writing it down. | cycle 63 ATTEMPT 2 PASSED THE GATE (sonnet). The retry replaced the false corner-to-corner observable with a border-line-vs-body-row-edge one: the reader compares the right-hand bar on the phase/illuminated/hemisphere rows against the right end of the top and bottom lines. Conductor gate authored independently at verification time and run over 368 frames (every 6 h across 2026-01-01..2026-02-15, both hemispheres), measuring display width from unicodedata UCD 15.0.0 under both width policies: ambiguous=1 -> every row 34 cols, named-row bar and both corners all at col 33 (aligned, reader correctly concludes UNAFFECTED) on 368/368 frames; ambiguous=2 -> border rows 68 cols, named rows 36 cols, bar at col 34 vs corners at col 66, i.e. 32 columns short (reader correctly concludes AFFECTED) on 368/368 frames. Zero frames where either branch misleads. Diff was a pure 7-line addition (7/0 README.md), so nothing retained was deleted or weakened. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-063-verify-t151.txt (plus -v1.txt, the conductor's own miscalibrated first pass).

So the correct output is a PIN plus a written caveat, not a re-tune. Same disposition, and the same reasoning, as this run's KI-5 call: pinning a measured boundary in a test converts a prose-only caveat into a machine-checked one at S-effort, and the defect can no longer drift silently.
